stem:
Sia puts vegetable peels and leftover food into a covered compost pit in the garden.

Which claim correctly explains how microorganisms can turn that waste into something useful and leave cleaner surroundings?

options.text: Microorganisms break down the plant and animal waste into manure that enriches soil and reduces leftover rubbish.
Microorganisms produce biogas from waste in an open, well-aerated heap.
Waste becomes manure on its own, which then attracts microorganisms to feed on it.
Soil microorganisms turn plastic wrappers into nutrient-rich manure.

teacher.key_rationale: Microbes decompose plant and animal waste into useful manure and cleaner surroundings. Biogas needs sealed anaerobic conditions, manure does not form first then summon microbes, and plastic is outside that manure process.
